# Clawd Wars

> A native macOS app (Swift + AppKit, no dependencies) that shows running Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI sessions as pixel-art Star Wars characters on the desktop or in a window. Every session and subagent is a hero or a villain (one shared cast; with two AIs running they take opposite sides); they fight while they work. Status comes from Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI hooks (same hook binary, `--assistant codex|qwen|gemini|copilot` and `--event <name>`; per-AI config in `HookInstaller.OtherAI`, payloads translated by `StatusStore.normalize`). Every sprite, effect, location and the app icon are drawn in code — there are no image assets.

## Build and run

- Requirements: macOS 13+, Swift 6.2+ from either the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) or Xcode, compiled in Swift 5 language mode. No third-party dependencies. Signing falls back to ad-hoc, which is fine locally (macOS then drops the Accessibility grant on every rebuild). The README's "Building from source" section covers the setup errors: no developer path, Xcode license, wrong `xcode-select` toolchain.
- The type checker's limit on a single expression is fixed, not timed, so a faster machine or a retry won't get past it. When the build fails with "unable to type-check this expression in reasonable time", the other errors in that file (`cannot infer contextual base`, key paths, `Float16` operators) all come from that one expression. Fix it by stating types: array literals of hex colours as `[Int]`, angles and closure parameters as `Double`. Write new art code the same way. Long untyped literal arrays piped through `.map`, and `.pi` arithmetic without an annotated `let`, are what trip it.
- `./build.sh` compiles with `swiftc` (no Xcode project, no SwiftPM), signs, installs `/Applications/Clawd Wars.app`, runs `--update-hooks` (refreshes only the AIs already connected; it never connects a new one, the app asks for that) and launches it. `./build.sh --no-hooks` skips the hooks. `./build.sh --no-install` builds, quits any running copy (only one runs at a time) and launches `build/Clawd Wars.app`: no copy to /Applications, no hook refresh (a build/ copy never takes over working hooks, see `HookInstaller.repairMoved`). `--install-hooks` connects every installed AI (Claude Code, Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI). An installed AI you don't connect can be waved off with the banner's × or "Don't Remind Me About …" (`OverlayController.ignoredHooks`).
- `./release.sh <version>` builds a universal (arm64 + x86_64) release zip, publishes it as a GitHub release and updates the Homebrew cask in `rodclemen/homebrew-tap`.
- There are no unit tests; `<app binary> --chaos=90` is a randomized soak test of the layout (characters on screen, nobody stuck walking, nobody missing, labels on screen and not overlapping) that prints a report and exits non-zero on violations. Check visuals with the frame dump: `CLAWD_SHOT=/tmp/shot.png <app binary> --playground=0,1 --agents=0,1 [--mood=idle] [--ais=claude,codex] [--projects=a,a,b]` writes the rendered scene every 5 s (window mode is the default; `defaults write <domain> windowMode -bool false` for the desktop). `CLAWD_HOVER=<actor key>` fakes a hover; `VADER_DEBUG=1` logs layout and fight roles.
- `Tools/RenderDocs` renders `docs/roster.png`, `docs/locations.png` and `docs/social-preview.png`; `Tools/MakeIcon` renders `Resources/AppIcon.png`.

## Code map

- [Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift](Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift): the state shared by hook and app (`~/.claude/vader-status/state.json`, written under `flock`). Turns hook events into session/agent records, assigns villains (random, Vader and Kylo never back to back) and heroes, and builds `SessionSnapshot`s. A session's project name comes from its live process cwd (not the hooks' copy, which goes stale after a folder rename): the git remote's repo name, else the folder name.
- [Sources/Shared/Processes.swift](Sources/Shared/Processes.swift): finds `claude`, `codex`, `qwen`, `gemini` and `copilot` processes, their cwd, start time and CPU time (sessions without hooks, dead-session pruning, "busy" detection).
- [Sources/Shared/GitRemote.swift](Sources/Shared/GitRemote.swift): reads a project's remote from `.git/config` on disk (no network; walks up from subfolders, follows worktrees), giving the repo name and host label for the card pill. Cached per cwd, re-read every 5 s.
- [Sources/Hook/main.swift](Sources/Hook/main.swift): the `clawd-wars-hook` binary Claude Code runs; reads hook JSON from stdin, never prints, always exits 0.
- [Sources/App/Overlay.swift](Sources/App/Overlay.swift): `OverlayController` — refresh loop, status debounce, fight pairing and formation layout, walking, labels, bubbles, hover cards, menus (incl. the menu bar helmet: menu on click, hide/show on double-click), window-mode glue, frame dump. `OverlayView.render` draws a list of `DrawItem`s (screen coordinates).
- [Sources/App/Characters.swift](Sources/App/Characters.swift): the shared Clawd body, saber choreography (`kataPose`, `duelPose`), blasters, and all heroes (`Companion`).
- [Sources/App/Leaders.swift](Sources/App/Leaders.swift): all villains (`Leader`), weapons, `FightRole`s, fight effects (`drawFightFX`, `Fighter`), speech bubbles.
- [Sources/App/Recruits.swift](Sources/App/Recruits.swift): the second wave of the cast: the heroes from Jar Jar on (`drawJarJar`…`drawGonk`) and the villains from Sebulba on (costumes `drawLeader` dresses). New cast members are appended to `Leader`/`Companion` (ids are stored), and `StatusStore.leaderCount`/`companionCount` must match. `StatusStore.agentOnly` (the MSE-6 and the ID9) never leads a session: use `leaderCast` for session pools.
- [Sources/App/Locations.swift](Sources/App/Locations.swift) and [Sources/App/Cantina.swift](Sources/App/Cantina.swift): window-mode scenes (`Location`), static layer + animated layer, plus drawing helpers.
- [Sources/App/WindowMode.swift](Sources/App/WindowMode.swift): the window (themed header, scene strip, per-Claude cards, auto height). `RoomView` holds the location's static picture behind `SceneView`.
- [Sources/App/SpriteLayers.swift](Sources/App/SpriteLayers.swift): shows a frame's `DrawItem`s as reused Core Animation layers (GPU scaling, nearest-neighbour; text cached as images), for both the window's scene and the desktop crew. `OverlayView.render` is still the Core Graphics path, used for text images and `CLAWD_SHOT`.
- [Sources/App/Jump.swift](Sources/App/Jump.swift): click-to-jump to a session's terminal tab or editor window (AppleScript for Terminal/iTerm2, Accessibility API for VS Code/Cursor incl. native tabs).
- Hook health: `OverlayController.refreshStatus` lists `hookIssues` for AIs that are installed (`HookInstaller.claudeAvailable` / `available`) but not hooked up, or whose sessions ran a turn without reporting (`SessionSnapshot.hookSilent`, e.g. Codex hooks not approved in `/hooks`). These feed the banner, ⚠︎ menu items and a one-per-session notification.
- [Sources/Saver/SaverView.swift](Sources/Saver/SaverView.swift): the screen saver (`Clawd Wars.saver`, built by build.sh into the app's Resources), and the window's third view (the app compiles it in too: `ClawdWindow.board`, fed `OverlayController.saverFeed` through `feedSource`, `inWindow` for no clock, a bigger place name and hover-to-enlarge cards). A `ScreenSaverView` running sandboxed in macOS's `legacyScreenSaver` host: the location at full screen (about 270 art pixels tall), the crew with the window's fight pairing, name tags over every head (`Cast.drawnTop` / `drawnProfile` measure each sprite, shared with the window's labels; the focused session's tag is 15% larger), one card per session floating above the crew in its project's colour with a beam to its name (`board`), the clock and an event ticker, all as Core Animation layers. Every 10 minutes (`shiftEvery`) it wipes to another location (`travel`, `Wipe` in Locations.swift, shared with the window) and swaps the clock and place name and lifts the cards and tags (`shifted`) against burn-in. It reads only [Sources/Shared/SaverFeed.swift](Sources/Shared/SaverFeed.swift)'s `screensaver.json` in `~/Library/Application Support/Clawd Wars/`, which the running app writes about once a second while the saver is installed (`OverlayController.publishSaverFeed`); stale = Clawd Wars isn't running (never in the window, which hands it the feed directly), and the saver puts on a show instead: a made-up crew of 4–6 (`cast(for:)`, up to two of them agents, light against dark, a local or two of the place among them) with name tags but no cards, off somewhere new every 3 minutes (`demoEvery`), and a quiet "isn't running" line under the place name. Inside the sandbox `NSHomeDirectory()` is the container: use `SaverFeed.home`. [Sources/App/SaverInstaller.swift](Sources/App/SaverInstaller.swift) copies it into `~/Library/Screen Savers`, refreshes that copy when the app's differs (code or sealed resources), and removes it. Locations draw extra scenery only on tall canvases, so the window's strip is unchanged.
- [Sources/App/Greedo.swift](Sources/App/Greedo.swift): Han shoots first. `GreedoShot` has the timeline (the bolt lands, a backward somersault onto his back, 3 s down, rolling back up, his line, walking back), Greedo's pose and sprite (`PixelCanvas.rotated`, on a 112×72 canvas whose feet row sits like a standing sprite's), and the bolt FX. `OverlayController.buildItems` runs the clock (`greedoShot`, `nextGreedoShot`): it starts on one of Han's own shots, nobody ducks, Han lowers his blaster after the hit, and their lines go over their name tags. Desktop and window only, not the screen saver. `CLAWD_GREEDO_EVERY=<seconds>` forces it for testing, e.g. `--playground=0,14,1 --agents=1,0`.
- [Sources/App/Legend.swift](Sources/App/Legend.swift): Status Symbols (top level of the menu), the key to bubbles, poses, outline and label colours and banners. Icons come from the real drawing code (`drawLeader`, `drawBubble`, `drawFocusCaret`), so a new bubble kind or status should get a row here and in the README's table. Rows are custom views: macOS 27 menus ignore `NSMenuItem.image`.
- [Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift](Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift), [Sources/App/Accents.swift](Sources/App/Accents.swift), [Sources/App/Pixel.swift](Sources/App/Pixel.swift) (the `PixelCanvas` all art is drawn on).

## Conventions

- Sprites are 72×52 canvases facing right; the body is x 18…37, y 26…37, feet end at row 43, the hand pivot is (41.5, 34.5). Characters facing left are mirrored by the renderer. `C(0xRRGGBB)` makes a colour; `canvas.pattern(x, y, rows, palette)` draws string art.
- Adding a villain: a case in `Leader` (name, weapon, headTop, optional muzzle), a `draw…` costume, a home in `Location.home(of:)`, a Playground weapon label in `Overlay.swift`, and bump `StatusStore.leaderCount`. Heroes likewise with `Companion` and `companionCount`.
- Cast ids: villains are `Leader.rawValue` (< 100), heroes `100 + Companion.rawValue`; `Cast` (Sources/App/Cast.swift) wraps both and draws either as a session or an agent. Side rules live in `StatusStore.side(for:in:)`, `nextLeader` and `nextAgentCast`.
- Per-AI look lives in `AIStyle` (Sources/App/Accents.swift): outline colour (never dark) and list order. `Actor.assistant` carries it to sprites; cards and the menu group by it.
- Fight rules: Han and Greedo always face off first, whether each is a Claude or an agent (in `relayout` and the screen saver's `crew`); then Claudes fight Claudes, agents fight agents, a leftover Claude and agent fight each other, anyone else left over cheers; unarmed characters are bystanders.
- Commits follow Conventional Commits; every change gets a CHANGELOG entry.
